memory_candidates.content: Before attributing a validate-state.sh / check-task-references.sh failure to your own task's write, `git stash` (or diff against the pre-task commit) and re-run the same gate. Repo-wide gates that already fail for unrelated, pre-existing reasons are common in a large, long-lived specs/state.json; the discipline is to isolate the delta your own write introduced (grep the diff for your new entry's project_number, or confirm every file you touched is excluded from the scanner's scope) rather than either blocking on a pre-existing failure or silently claiming a clean exit code you did not actually get.

.claude/scripts/task-lock.sh scope-acquire/scope-release take a positional session_id/token argument with no flag parsing -- passing '--help' (or any leading-dash string) as the argument is silently accepted as a literal session_id and actually acquires (or attempts to release) the mutex rather than printing usage. If this happens, immediately scope-release using the printed token before retrying with the real session_id; do not assume a flag-shaped argument was rejected.

For a cross-repository hand-off that must survive task renumbering on either side, name every must-land result by fully-qualified declaration name (e.g. `Namespace.Module.theorem_name`) rather than by task number, and separately name which consumer tasks are already satisfied and should not wait. Pair this with an explicit 'orthogonal, not part of this programme' section for tasks that look related but need a different result the programme does not supply -- this prevents a downstream task from waiting on the wrong thing.
